decisions.statement: A deploy names one thing.
Every kind a deploy puts up is a service.
Which kind of thing a slug names settles how that thing is put up.
A slug a web app page and an ios app page both carry is refused rather than chosen between.
A slug no kind this puts up carries is refused by naming every kind.
A workstation service is put up with nothing built.
A deploy reaches every workstation service's units at once rather than one service's.
The parts a deploy is made of are read from the page rather than said on the call.
A deploy is made at one commit rather than at whatever HEAD is at the time.
A commit named on the call settles the commit a deploy is made at.
A call naming none is made at the commit HEAD is at, resolved to its hash.
The report names that hash before anything the kind itself says.
A deploy that finished keeps the commit beside the page it was read from.
A deploy that refused keeps the commit it refused at under its own key.
A deploy that refused keeps what it refused for under a key of its own.
A refusal kept is held to four thousand characters, and a longer one says it was cut.
A workstation service is put up without reaching any service to do it.
A workstation service's deploy keeps and reads that commit on disk beside the page.
A deploy of every other kind keeps and reads that commit through the pages.
What putting a thing up cost is kept beside the page that thing was read from.
What is counted is the putting up rather than the reading and judging before it.
A commit kept here is uncommitted, so no deploy lands a commit of its own.
A file another deploy is built from and this one is not leaves this one alone.
The checks stating they run on a deploy judge a deploy before anything is put up.
Those checks are run over what changed from the last deploy's commit to this one.
A check refusing a file a deploy is built from refuses that deploy.
The test proving a workstation service runs is judged wherever that service would restart.
A service whose test is refused leaves every unit and every tree as they were.
A workstation service with no such test beside its page refuses the deploy.
That refusal names each service, and the checks are run over nothing.
A commit named twice is refused rather than chosen between.
An ios app is put in front of people by this command.
A flag belonging to the other kind of app is refused rather than ignored.
A deploy runs under the ceiling its page states unless the call says otherwise.
A deploy told to be measured runs under no ceiling.
A cluster service is put up with the image it runs built where the registry lacks it.
A container recipe is put up as its image in the registry and nothing else.
An ios app told to go on a simulator is installed there rather than handed to Apple.
An ios app told to go on a phone is installed there rather than handed to Apple.
A call naming both places to install to is refused rather than chosen between.
An inference service is put up as an environment and an agent on the machine its page names.
A host already holding an inference service unchanged is applied to by nothing.
An inference service its page says is not to be running is torn off its host.
An ESO addon is compiled to Lua and put where the game reads it by this command.
An addon that will not compile leaves the game's folder as it was.
A folder in the game nothing here wrote is never deleted on missing evidence.
A web app whose page states an addon bundle image publishes that bundle first.
The bundle is published before the web app serving it is put up.
A deploy is built from a tree pinned at the commit rather than from the checkout.
Each thing a deploy puts up is named as soon as that thing reaches a machine.
A deploy that threw part way names those things in its refusal.
A deploy refused without a throw names them in its refusal too.
It names them in the sentence every command's refusal names them in.
A deploy that threw before any of them says so rather than saying it may be partial.
The putting up a deploy runs is handed in.
A thing already being put up refuses a second deploy of that thing rather than waiting on it.
A deploy that puts up from the workstation waits for the memory a landing starts on first.
A deploy of a cluster service, a container recipe or a web app runs in the cluster.
A deploy of every other kind runs on the workstation.
A cluster foundation is put up as the manifests its page names and nothing else.
A foundation's deploy runs on the workstation rather than in the cluster.
The account a cluster run deploys under is part of that foundation, so no cluster run mends it.
A deploy that is itself the run in the cluster puts up there rather than sending another run.
A run in the cluster is known by what the pod states in its environment.
What the run in the cluster said is what a deploy sent there reports.
A deploy sent to the cluster is held apart from a second deploy of that thing.

definition: the command putting up what a page describes
